nodes.title: The second-candidate gate is wired on the default path; 'evidence' was absent because the price was zero, not because the branch was dead
nodes.body:
gap-cand-001 asked whether the repaired gate changes round behaviour or whether `autoCandidateMode` is the only thing that ever acts -- the tell being that `candidateModeSource` is 'evidence' in 0 of 241 recorded rounds.

Reading src/runtime/round.js:1043-1075: the evidence branch is gated on `candidateMode === 'parallel'` and `secondCandidate !== 'always'`, and `candidateMode` defaults to 'parallel' (source 'default'). So the branch runs on every campaign that has not configured otherwise -- no `autoCandidateMode` needed. `autoCandidateMode` governs a different decision (whether to infer `cascade` from the record), not this one.

The absence of 'evidence' therefore had exactly one cause: `secondCandidateGate` never returned admit:false, because the tail it priced was identically zero (exp-cand-003). A dead-looking branch and a branch whose condition is never satisfied look the same in the log.

Evidence that it now fires:
* tests/balance/second-candidate-gate.test.mjs case 2 drives real runRound with three losing rounds whose attempts carry measured durations, and asserts candidatesPlanned=1, candidateModeSource='evidence', secondCandidate.tailMs>0 (4/4).
* e74 replays 114 priceable historical rounds: refusals go 0 -> 23, declining 6,584 s (1.83 h) of hedging across 8 campaigns.

The residual is that no live campaign has recorded 'evidence' yet -- the fix is loaded but no campaign has run since. That is a fact about the clock, not about the wiring, and one round of any campaign with a losing record will produce the first instance.

edges.note: answers the gap: wired on the default path, absent only because the price was zero
